case.pattern_description: Four online card-not-present authorizations on the same card within 30 minutes, each deliberately priced just under a $500 round authorization threshold ($456.96-$488.04), split across two 'New'-flagged devices, two email domains and two billing regions (264 and 476, one pair behind a transparent proxy). The splitting and threshold-hugging looks like an attempt to keep every single charge below an authorization/review limit while extracting ~$1.9k in one sitting, rather than a plain CNP burst.

evidence.claim: Cardholder C07297 explicitly disputes the $482.12 charge 3476682 ('I never made this purchase').
Four online product-C authorizations in 30 minutes (20:00-20:30 on 2016-11-21) all priced just under $500: 478.95, 456.96, 488.04, 482.12; combined exposure $1,906.07.
Baseline over 180d: 199 txns, 194 in-person / 5 online, products W=194 vs C=3; online share 2.5%, product C share 1.5%. The episode is entirely online product C.
Each episode amount is ~4x the card mean of $116.73 (amount_vs_mean 3.91-4.18, amount_z 2.71), though below the card max of $1,104.

All four online txns carry device_new_flag 'New'; 3476633 and 3476665 also run behind a TRANSPARENT proxy with a yahoo.com email from region 476, while 3476602/3476682 use a Windows 7 / IE 11 desktop with gmail.com from region 264.

Normal in-person home activity continues around the burst (3474057 $226.02 in region 264 on 11-20, 3477578 $82.97 in region 315 on 11-22; home_activity_within_48h = 7), so the card itself remained with the cardholder while the number was used online.
No rare shared device link: rare_shared_devices_total = 0 and no cards linked by device; region 264 newcomer fraud rate 0.10 equals the base rate, so no ring evidence.
Recurring check fails: only one prior same-amount txn (3476602, same night), a single month, looks_monthly = false, so R7 does not apply.
Policy §3a: exposure exceeds $1,000 and the pattern is undocumented/coordinated (R9), so a report accompanies the case.

Semantically similar closed cases CC-4027, CC-2537, CC-2937, CC-4437 were all cleared after the cardholder confirmed a single large purchase; none involved a disputed multi-transaction sub-threshold burst, so they do not offset the structural evidence here.

case.summary: C07297 disputes a $482.12 online charge (3476682), and the graph shows it is the last of four online product-C authorizations fired between 20:00 and 20:30 on 2016-11-21, each just under $500 ($478.95, $456.96, $488.04, $482.12; $1,906.07 total). The card's 180-day baseline is 97.5% in-person, product W, averaging $116.73, so the channel, product and amounts are all out of character. All four carry a 'New' device flag, two of them behind a TRANSPARENT proxy with a different email domain and billing region (476), while genuine in-person spending continued in the cardholder's home regions before and after the burst. No rare shared device or region-ring link exists, so this looks like a single-card compromise where charges were deliberately kept under a round authorization threshold — coordinated/repeated abuse that fits none of the five documented patterns (R9). Recommend BLOCK_CARD, CREATE_CASE and FILE_REPORT (exposure > $1,000, undocumented pattern) with ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST.

sar.narrative: This report concerns apparent unauthorized card-not-present activity on card C07297-K1, held by cardholder C07297, in which four online authorizations were deliberately priced just below a $500 round authorization threshold, totaling $1,906.07. On 2016-11-21 between 20:00 and 20:30, four online product-C authorizations were posted to the card: transaction 3476602 at 20:00 for $478.95, transaction 3476633 at 20:10 for $456.96, transaction 3476665 at 20:24 for $488.04, and transaction 3476682 at 20:30 for $482.12. The cardholder contacted the bank and explicitly disputed the $482.12 charge 3476682, stating they never made the purchase. All four authorizations carried a 'New' device flag; transactions 3476602 and 3476682 originated from a Windows 7 / Internet Explorer 11 desktop using a gmail.com email address billed to region 264, while transactions 3476633 and 3476665 ran behind a TRANSPARENT proxy using a yahoo.com email address billed to region 476. The card's 180-day baseline consists of 199 transactions, 194 in person and only 5 online, with 194 product W against 3 product C, so the online channel (2.5% of history) and product C (1.5% of history) are both out of character, and each episode amount is approximately four times the card mean of $116.73 (amount_z 2.71). Genuine in-person spending continued around the burst, including transaction 3474057 for $226.02 in region 264 on 2016-11-20 and transaction 3477578 for $82.97 in region 315 on 2016-11-22, with home_activity_within_48h of 7, indicating the physical card remained with the cardholder while the card number was used online. The method of operation was the splitting of roughly $1.9k of spend in a single sitting into four charges each held under $500 and spread across two newly seen devices, two email domains and two billing regions, consistent with an attempt to keep every charge below an authorization or review limit. No ring indicators were found: rare_shared_devices_total is 0, no other cards are linked by device, and the region 264 newcomer fraud rate of 0.10 equals the base rate. Recurring-payment checks do not apply, as the only prior same-amount transaction (3476602) occurred the same night and the activity is confined to a single month. Semantically similar closed cases CC-4027, CC-2537, CC-2937 and CC-4437 were cleared only after cardholders confirmed a single large purchase and do not match this disputed multi-transaction sub-threshold burst. Total exposure is $1,906.07; the bank blocked card C07297-K1, opened a fraud case, escalated the matter to an analyst, and is filing this report because exposure exceeds $1,000 and the pattern is undocumented and coordinated.
